result.title: Flagging Batch Shift in Flow Cytometry using Jeffreys Divergence between Gaussian Mixtures
result.summary: Machine learning models for clinical flow cytometry are usually evaluated on data drawn from their training distribution. In routine practice, however, acquisition conditions and reagents may change, potentially making predictions unreliable without warning. We propose a model agnostic criterion for prediction reliability based on a notion of distance from the training distribution: each patient sample is represented by a Gaussian mixture model, and its Jeffreys divergence to a reference fitted on the training data is estimated using Monte Carlo integration. We illustrate our approach on real-life shifted cohorts of acute myeloid leukaemia patients, using a classifier trained to predict NPM1 mutation status. First, we show graphically and statistically that pairwise divergences capture acquisition cohort structure. We then calibrate a rejection threshold on a subset of shifted cohort samples and evaluate it on held-out subjects. Across 20 runs, the misclassification rate of rejected samples was 2.5 times larger than for retained samples. These results suggest that input divergence can help identify unreliable predictions, providing a strong candidate component for abstention frameworks, along with quality control measures and classifier confidence.

AI.brief_summary: 提出模型无关的预测可靠性判据：将每个病人样本表示为高斯混合模型，用蒙特卡洛估计其与训练集参考分布的 Jeffreys 散度，并校准拒绝阈值以标记不可靠预测，在急性髓系白血病队列上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 以输入分布散度作为弃权或停止信号，可能为 LVR 中「证据是否充足、是否继续获取视觉证据或终止推理」的门控设计提供借鉴线索，可供核查其阈值校准思路能否迁移到多步推理状态。
